title: ChatGPT's favourite sentence #shorts
description:
ChatGPT wrote all of these. It's not a tool, it's a teammate. It's not a change, it's a revolution. It's not software, it's a partner.

It is the same sentence every time, and you have already read it today.

Wikipedia keeps an advice page called Signs of AI writing, maintained by the volunteers of WikiProject AI Cleanup. They use it to spot articles a chatbot wrote. It carries 78 named tells, and this construction is one of them. Its section is called Negative parallelisms, with three variants underneath: "Not just X, but also Y", "Not X, but Y", and "X rather than Y".

ChatGPT writes it because it sounds clever. The sentence knocks down a wrong idea, then says the right one. That feels like thinking. It is only a pattern.

So it turns up everywhere. In captions. In product updates. In apologies from companies that never wrote a word themselves. And in your sent folder, because you asked ChatGPT to tidy an email, it handed that sentence back, the email sounded sharp, and you sent it.

From now on you will spot it. In your feed. In a newsletter. Halfway down your own draft. When you spot it, delete it. The plain sentence underneath is what you actually meant, and that one sounds like you.

Source: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing, an advice page from WikiProject AI Cleanup (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Signs_of_AI_writing), section "Negative parallelisms". The count of 78 tells was measured off the page on 1 September 2026.
